title: Schumann’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Schumann’s Missing Symphony (work id schumann-symphony-1)

A four-movement symphony in F minor that ends in F major, a key Schumann did not use for a symphony. New music in his manner; no theme is taken from him.

Orchestra (13 staves, sounding pitch): pairs of flutes, oboes, clarinets and bassoons; four horns and two trumpets (valve instruments, written chromatically); three trombones; timpani in F and C; strings.

The whole work grows from a four-note motto: F, A flat, G, C (up a third, down a step, up a fourth).
I. Ziemlich langsam – Lebhaft, F minor. The horns state the motto over trombones; the fast movement turns it into an impetuous dotted theme, sets a long clarinet melody in A flat against it, and closes its exposition with the motto triumphant in the major. Development with a fugato on the motto; the reprise brings the second theme in F major, but the coda falls back to the minor.
II. Romanze, D flat major, 3/4: a song for clarinet and bassoon in octaves over plucked strings, around a chorale for the trombones built on the motto.
III. Scherzo, F minor, with cross-rhythms, and a gentler Trio in D flat.
IV. Langsam – Lebhaft, F major: a slow bridge on the motto, then a finale whose march-like theme is the motto in the major, with a broad chorale at the climax and a faster coda.

Target length about sixteen minutes. Stylistic approach: cyclic motto, dotted and syncopated rhythms, thick doubling, a brass chorale. Compromise known from the start: tunes, motto transformations, the fugato, chorale and the chord of every bar are written by hand; a program scores quiet, woodwind and full-orchestra passages from the chord plan.

entries.speaker: Draft publication
entries.text:
Published live draft revision 1 with this public change note:
First playable draft: the whole first movement — the motto in horns and trombones, an impetuous F minor Lebhaft made from it, a clarinet second theme in A flat, a fugato on the motto in the development, and a coda that falls back to the minor.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m1, m2, m3, m4: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. All four movements. Fixes after the first build of II–IV: a G natural that should have been G flat in the Scherzo's second part, nine parallel octaves/fifths between first violins and bass (three of them under the Finale's chorale, whose bass was re-harmonised), and a held note against the second theme's bass.

entries.speaker: Draft publication
entries.text:
Published live draft revision 2 with this public change note:
First complete draft: added the Romanze in D flat with its trombone chorale, the F minor Scherzo and Trio, and the Finale in F major, which turns the motto and first-movement theme to the major and recalls the second theme. A revision pass follows.

entries.speaker: Draft publication
entries.text:
Published live draft revision 3 with this public change note:
Revision: the oboe joins the violins in the Romanze's return, and the Scherzo's reprise opens in clarinet and flute. This revision matches the published score.
